newsitem.title: UK: Metals make slow start on LME, copper steadier.
newsitem.headline: Metals make slow start on LME, copper steadier.

text.p: LME pre-market trading got off to a slow start on Friday, with the market tending to wind down ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Copper prices were steadier, absorbing a 7,800 tonne increase in warehouse stocks - the third successive bumper daily rise. However, this had been expected, traders said.
"This is no surprise - we had expected around 50,000 tonnes to come in by the end of July," one trader said.
The increase for this week is 42,025 tonnes, taking the overall total to 181,150 tonnes. Since the start of the year LME copper stocks have increased by some 56 percent.
Three months traded recently at $2,290 a tonne, up $10 from the Thursday kerb. The cash/threes backwardation was at $115/125.
Elsewhere aluminium prices were slightly higher at $1,581, up $2 a tonne. Inventories fell by 2,550 tonnes.
Zinc gained $7 to trade at $1,518, helped by a 2,850-tonne stock draw, while sister metal lead was $4 steadier at $645.
Tin and nickel were indicated at slightly steadier levels of $5,440/50 and $6,830/50 a tonne respectively.
